sentences.text: This review covers wellbore 15/9-F-9 A, a sidetrack-type well in the F-segment of the Volve field in the Norwegian North Sea.

No data tools were available when this review was written, so the review states no measured figures: hole sizes, depths, dates, lost-time hours and rates are all left for verification against the field database.
Any figure that is added later should be tied to its source report and checked against the daily drilling reports before the review is issued.
The review of hole sections should cover each section's start and end depth, its new hole drilled, its hole size and its casing shoe position.
Section boundaries should be reconciled with the casing program so that each casing shoe is matched to the section it closes.
Drilling performance should be judged by section, comparing the achieved rate of penetration with the planned rate and noting where connections, tripping or wireline work dominated the time.

Lost time should be split into primary and possible tiers, and each tier should be traced to the activity codes that explain it, so that equipment, well control and operational causes can be separated.
Real-time curve statistics were not used in this review and should not be read as supporting any conclusion here.
The hole-section table, the lost-time breakdown and the campaign timeline still need to be populated from the database before this review can be used for lessons learned.
The reviewer should confirm the final total depth and the completion status against the well's end-of-well documentation.
